exchanges: I returned yesterday from Thomson’s marriage at Bath, he has left for India via France. I spoke to Bennett about the Linn. Soc. & you are to have any reasonable number of volumes for a reasonable time but please do not talk about it. We are I hope really about to have a reform in the Linnean & get a first rate Natural History Journal established; I have been moving heaven & earth to get the Linnean to organize it & enlist contributors & subscribers & have such a thorough reform as shall bring us members, attendance & subscriptions— Natural Science languishes in this country for support & plenty are ready to

Very many thanks about Bennett; I will keep profoundly quiet, like a well trained rogue.— I honour all your zeal about the new Journal, & heartily hope it success. I shd. be very glad to contribute anything, but I do not know how it is, that I never have short communications of any kind.—
